papers.title: st2traj: deconvolution-informed trajectory inference for multi-timepoint spatial transcriptomics
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Multi-timepoint spatial transcriptomics enables study of developmental processes in native tissue context, but cell-state mixtures within spots and lack of direct spatial correspondence across sections complicate trajectory inference and biological interpretation. Results st2traj is a deconvolution-informed trajectory framework using spot-state composition for multi-timepoint spatial trajectory inference. In a human heart pseudo-spot benchmark, DECODE showed competitive and balanced performance among five deconvolution methods. In multi-timepoint human heart data, unscaled DECODE-derived proportions produced smoother trajectory fields and stronger agreement with expression-derived marker programs than normalized spot-level expression. st2traj also showed greater spatial coherence than spaTrack, while exploratory comparisons with moscot and CASCAT revealed complementary method-specific strengths. Application to an independent chicken heart dataset recovered stage-associated trajectory changes across D7, D10, and D14. Availability and Implementation Source code: https://github.com/xiaoxiaoxier/st2traj . Software v0.1.0 and processed data are archived at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21487030 and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21502094

**摘要**  
多时间点空间转录组学技术能够让我们在天然组织环境中研究发育过程，但样本中存在的细胞状态混合现象以及不同切片之间缺乏直接的空间对应关系，这些因素都给轨迹推断和生物学解释带来了困难。本研究开发的**st2traj**是一种基于去卷积技术的轨迹分析工具，它利用样本中各细胞状态的组成信息来推断多时间点下的空间发育轨迹。在人类心脏样本的测试中，**DECODE**在五种去卷积方法中表现出了优异且均衡的性能；而在实际的人类心脏数据应用中，未经归一化的**DECODE**计算结果所生成的轨迹图更加平滑，其与表达谱数据的匹配程度也优于经过归一化处理的样本数据。此外，**st2traj**在空间一致性方面也优于其他类似工具；与**moscot**和**CASCAT**的对比实验进一步证明了这些方法各自具有的优势。当将该技术应用于独立的鸡心脏数据集时，研究人员成功揭示了D7、D10和D14这三个发育阶段中相关组织的轨迹变化规律。

papers.title: TargetPrior: A miRNA-Signature Embedded Evolutionary Learning Framework for Prioritizing Drug Targets in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Prioritizing therapeutic targets from high-dimensional transcriptomic profiles is hindered by the underdetermined nature of the p ≫ n setting. While miRNA signatures can inform target prioritization, conventional accuracy-driven methods may yield unstable predictive signatures, reducing downstream network reliability and topology-guided candidate ranking. Results We propose TargetPrior, a stability-aware evolutionary learning framework in which EL-CAML derives reproducible miRNA anchors from relapse-associated transcriptomic variation for candidate target prioritization. In childhood acute myeloid leukemia (CAML), EL-CAML identifies a parsimonious 18-miRNA continuous relapse-risk signature and 10 complementary stability-supported biomarkers, yielding 28 miRNAs for literature-curated miRNA–gene network construction. Repeated perturbation analysis supported the stability of high-frequency miRNAs, while analysis of the independent GSE196886 cell-sorted small RNA-seq dataset identified cell-population-specific expression differences. Benchmarking against an expanded set of clinically and biologically supported AML target references showed stronger early-rank retrieval than network-only and statistical approaches. TargetPrior is presented as a computational proof-of-concept for generating prioritized therapeutic hypotheses, rather than as a universal target-discovery solution. **摘要**  
在高维转录组数据中筛选治疗靶点时，由于“p ≫ n”的数据特性，目标选择的准确性往往受到限制。虽然miRNA特征谱有助于确定优先靶点，但传统的基于精确度的方法可能产生不稳定的预测结果，从而影响后续的网络分析及候选靶点的排序效率。  

**研究方法**  
我们提出了TargetPrior这一基于进化学习的方法框架。该框架通过EL-CAML算法，从与疾病复发相关的转录组变异中筛选出可靠的miRNA标志物，进而用于优先选择治疗靶点。在儿童急性髓系白血病的数据分析中，EL-CAML识别出了18个与复发风险密切相关的miRNA标志物，以及10个能够进一步验证这些标志物稳定性的生物标志物；最终获得了28个miRNA，用于构建miRNA-基因网络。重复实验结果证实了这些高频表达miRNA的稳定性，而通过对独立的小RNA测序数据集的分析，还发现了不同细胞群体之间的表达差异。  

**实验效果**  
与现有的基于临床和生物学证据的AML靶点识别方法相比，TargetPrior在早期靶点筛选阶段的性能更为优异。该技术更像是一种用于生成优先治疗假设的计算工具，而非通用的靶点发现方案。  

**代码获取**  
相关代码可访问以下链接：https://github.com/NYCU-ICLAB/TargetPrior，并已存档于Zenodo平台。

papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Prioritizing therapeutic targets from high-dimensional transcriptomic profiles is hindered by the underdetermined nature of the p ≫ n setting. While miRNA signatures can inform target prioritization, conventional accuracy-driven methods may yield unstable predictive signatures, reducing downstream network reliability and topology-guided candidate ranking.

RESULTS: We propose TargetPrior, a stability-aware evolutionary learning framework in which EL-CAML derives reproducible miRNA anchors from relapse-associated transcriptomic variation for candidate target prioritization. In childhood acute myeloid leukemia (CAML), EL-CAML identifies a parsimonious 18-miRNA continuous relapse-risk signature and 10 complementary stability-supported biomarkers, yielding 28 miRNAs for literature-curated miRNA-gene network construction. Repeated perturbation analysis supported the stability of high-frequency miRNAs, while analysis of the independent GSE196886 cell-sorted small RNA-seq dataset identified cell-population-specific expression differences. Benchmarking against an expanded set of clinically and biologically supported AML target references showed stronger early-rank retrieval than network-only and statistical approaches. TargetPrior is presented as a computational proof-of-concept for generating prioritized therapeutic hypotheses, rather than as a universal target-discovery solution.

AVAILABILITY: Code is available at: https://github.com/NYCU-ICLAB/TargetPrior and archived on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20394263).

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.title: Finetuning Foundation Models for Temporal Clinical Transcriptomics Data
papers.summary: Abstract Background Timeseries clinical transcriptomic datasets offer the opportunity to gain insights into the dynamics of disease mechanisms/treatment responses. However, their utility in uncovering temporal patterns is often limited by high noise levels and small sample sizes. Leveraging foundational gene embeddings and incorporating interaction information can help address these challenges, improve gene network analysis, and enable the detection of subtle changes that drive disease progression or drug response. Results We finetuned gene embeddings from foundation models using healthy tissue gene expression data and used them in temporal GNNs to model gene expression of responder and non-responders to treatment in 4 disease datasets - ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s disease, Alopecia Areata, and psoriasis. Application of our method to these datasets confirmed known mechanisms associated with drug action, and also identified key differences between activated and repressed pathways for responders and non-responders, including B-Cell activation and mitochondria-related activity in ulcerative colitis patients. Conclusion Finetuning gene embeddings from foundation models provides a richer context to model gene expression data compared to using them in their naive state. Even with smaller sample sizes, results from GNN-based temporal models outperform traditional methods by detecting known mechanisms of response and unraveling role of genes and mechanisms not known to be associated with response and non-response. Code Availability Code and data are available in a public GitHub repository - https://github.com/ Sanofi -Public/GNN-Timeseries

BACKGROUND: Timeseries clinical transcriptomic datasets offer the opportunity to gain insights into the dynamics of disease mechanisms/treatment responses. However, their utility in uncovering temporal patterns is often limited by high noise levels and small sample sizes. Leveraging foundational gene embeddings and incorporating interaction information can help address these challenges, improve gene network analysis, and enable the detection of subtle changes that drive disease progression or drug response.

RESULTS: We finetuned gene embeddings from foundation models using healthy tissue gene expression data and used them in temporal GNNs to model gene expression of responder and non-responders to treatment in 4 disease datasets - ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, Alopecia Areata, and psoriasis. Application of our method to these datasets confirmed known mechanisms associated with drug action, and also identified key differences between activated and repressed pathways for responders and non-responders, including B-Cell activation and mitochondria-related activity in ulcerative colitis patients.

CONCLUSION: Finetuning gene embeddings from foundation models provides a richer context to model gene expression data compared to using them in their naive state. Even with smaller sample sizes, results from GNN-based temporal models outperform traditional methods by detecting known mechanisms of response and unraveling role of genes and mechanisms not known to be associated with response and non-response.

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
时间序列临床转录组数据为研究疾病机制及治疗反应的动态变化提供了有力工具。然而，由于噪声水平较高且样本量较小，这些数据在揭示时间规律方面的作用往往受到限制。通过利用基础基因嵌入模型并结合基因相互作用信息，可以有效克服这些挑战，从而改进基因网络分析，进而检测出那些驱动疾病进展或药物反应的细微变化。  

**结果**  
我们利用健康组织的基因表达数据对基础基因嵌入模型进行了优化，并将其应用于4种疾病的数据集中，以模拟治疗响应者与非响应者的基因表达变化。这些疾病包括溃疡性结肠炎、克罗恩病、斑秃和银屑病。研究结果不仅验证了已知的药物作用机制，还发现了响应者与非响应者在基因通路激活程度上的关键差异——例如，在溃疡性结肠炎患者中，B细胞活化途径及线粒体相关功能存在显著差异。  

**结论**  
与直接使用未经优化的基础基因嵌入模型相比，通过对这些模型进行优化处理能为基因表达数据的分析提供更丰富的背景信息。即使在样本量较小的情况下，基于基因网络模型的时间序列分析方法也能显著优于传统方法——它不仅能检测出已知的反应机制，还能揭示那些此前未被认为与疾病响应相关的基因及作用途径。  

**代码与数据来源**  
相关代码及数据可访问公共GitHub仓库：  
https://github.com/Sanofi-Public/GNN-Timeseries

结果：我们利用健康组织的基因表达数据对基础基因嵌入模型进行了优化调整，随后将其应用于4种疾病数据集（溃疡性结肠炎、克罗恩病、斑秃和银屑病），通过时间序列图谱神经网络来分析治疗响应者与非响应者的基因表达模式。该方法的应用不仅验证了已知的药物作用机制，还揭示了响应者与非响应者在基因通路激活程度上的关键差异——例如，在溃疡性结肠炎患者中，B细胞活化途径及线粒体相关功能存在显著差异。

结论：与直接使用未经优化的基础基因嵌入模型相比，经过精细调整的基因嵌入模型能为基因表达数据分析提供更丰富的背景信息。即使在样本量较小的情况下，基于图谱神经网络的时间序列分析方法也能比传统方法更有效地识别已知的反应机制，并揭示那些此前未被认为与治疗响应相关的基因及作用途径。

papers.title: AdmixLD: Fast genome-scale inference of ancestry disequilibrium in hybrid zones
papers.summary: Abstract Summary Hybrid zones represent powerful natural systems for studying reproductive isolation and speciation. One key genomic signature of genetic incompatibilities and epistatic interactions is linkage disequilibrium (LD) — non-random associations between loci from different lineage backgrounds, generated by selection against maladaptive allele combinations. However, admixture alone induces strong genome-wide LD in hybrid populations, obscuring selection-driven signals. Here, we present AdmixLD, a fast, scalable C ++ tool for genome-wide LD scanning in hybrid zones that estimates LD using partial correlation to control for individual hybrid index. By removing admixture-driven covariance, AdmixLD enhances detection of locus-specific associations and enables genome-scale identification of candidate barrier loci and interacting genomic regions. Availability The software and its code source are available at https://github.com/yzfranci/AdmixLD , and scripts for the data analysis are available at https://github.com/yzfranci/AdmixLDAnalysis

all_papers.title: Finetuning Foundation Models for Temporal Clinical Transcriptomics Data
all_papers.summary: Abstract Background Timeseries clinical transcriptomic datasets offer the opportunity to gain insights into the dynamics of disease mechanisms/treatment responses. However, their utility in uncovering temporal patterns is often limited by high noise levels and small sample sizes. Leveraging foundational gene embeddings and incorporating interaction information can help address these challenges, improve gene network analysis, and enable the detection of subtle changes that drive disease progression or drug response. Results We finetuned gene embeddings from foundation models using healthy tissue gene expression data and used them in temporal GNNs to model gene expression of responder and non-responders to treatment in 4 disease datasets - ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s disease, Alopecia Areata, and psoriasis. Application of our method to these datasets confirmed known mechanisms associated with drug action, and also identified key differences between activated and repressed pathways for responders and non-responders, including B-Cell activation and mitochondria-related activity in ulcerative colitis patients. Conclusion Finetuning gene embeddings from foundation models provides a richer context to model gene expression data compared to using them in their naive state. Even with smaller sample sizes, results from GNN-based temporal models outperform traditional methods by detecting known mechanisms of response and unraveling role of genes and mechanisms not known to be associated with response and non-response. Code Availability Code and data are available in a public GitHub repository - https://github.com/ Sanofi -Public/GNN-Timeseries

RESULTS: We finetuned gene embeddings from foundation models using healthy tissue gene expression data and used them in temporal GNNs to model gene expression of responder and non-responders to treatment in 4 disease datasets - ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, Alopecia Areata, and psoriasis. **摘要**  
时间序列临床转录组数据为研究疾病机制及治疗反应的动态变化提供了有力工具。然而，由于噪声水平较高且样本量较小，这些数据在揭示时间规律方面的作用往往受到限制。通过利用基础基因嵌入模型并结合基因相互作用信息，可以有效克服这些挑战，从而改进基因网络分析，进而检测出那些驱动疾病进展或药物反应的细微变化。  

**结果**

all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
BACKGROUND: Timeseries clinical transcriptomic datasets offer the opportunity to gain insights into the dynamics of disease mechanisms/treatment responses. However, their utility in uncovering temporal patterns is often limited by high noise levels and small sample sizes. Leveraging foundational gene embeddings and incorporating interaction information can help address these challenges, improve gene network analysis, and enable the detection of subtle changes that drive disease progression or drug response.

RESULTS: We finetuned gene embeddings from foundation models using healthy tissue gene expression data and used them in temporal GNNs to model gene expression of responder and non-responders to treatment in 4 disease datasets - ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, Alopecia Areata, and psoriasis. Application of our method to these datasets confirmed known mechanisms associated with drug action, and also identified key differences between activated and repressed pathways for responders and non-responders, including B-Cell activation and mitochondria-related activity in ulcerative colitis patients.

CONCLUSION: Finetuning gene embeddings from foundation models provides a richer context to model gene expression data compared to using them in their naive state. Even with smaller sample sizes, results from GNN-based temporal models outperform traditional methods by detecting known mechanisms of response and unraveling role of genes and mechanisms not known to be associated with response and non-response.

CODE AVAILABILITY: Code and data are available in a public GitHub repository - https://github.com/Sanofi-Public/GNN-Timeseries. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20494035.

all_papers.title: st2traj: deconvolution-informed trajectory inference for multi-timepoint spatial transcriptomics
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Multi-timepoint spatial transcriptomics enables study of developmental processes in native tissue context, but cell-state mixtures within spots and lack of direct spatial correspondence across sections complicate trajectory inference and biological interpretation. Results st2traj is a deconvolution-informed trajectory framework using spot-state composition for multi-timepoint spatial trajectory inference. In a human heart pseudo-spot benchmark, DECODE showed competitive and balanced performance among five deconvolution methods. In multi-timepoint human heart data, unscaled DECODE-derived proportions produced smoother trajectory fields and stronger agreement with expression-derived marker programs than normalized spot-level expression. st2traj also showed greater spatial coherence than spaTrack, while exploratory comparisons with moscot and CASCAT revealed complementary method-specific strengths. Application to an independent chicken heart dataset recovered stage-associated trajectory changes across D7, D10, and D14. Availability and Implementation Source code: https://github.com/xiaoxiaoxier/st2traj . Software v0.1.0 and processed data are archived at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21487030 and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21502094

**摘要**  
多时间点空间转录组学技术能够让我们在天然组织环境中研究发育过程，但样本中存在的细胞状态混合现象以及不同切片之间缺乏直接的空间对应关系，这些因素都给轨迹推断和生物学解释带来了困难。本研究开发的**st2traj**是一种基于去卷积技术的轨迹分析工具，它利用样本中各细胞状态的组成信息来推断多时间点下的空间发育轨迹。在人类心脏样本的测试中，**DECODE**在五种去卷积方法中表现出了优异且均衡的性能；而在实际的人类心脏数据应用中，未经归一化的**DECODE**计算结果所生成的轨迹图更加平滑，其与表达谱数据的匹配程度也优于经过归一化处理的样本数据。此外，**st2traj**在空间一致性方面也优于其他类似工具；与**moscot**和**CASCAT**的对比实验进一步证明了这些方法各自具有的优势。当将该技术应用于独立的鸡心脏数据集时，研究人员成功揭示了D7、D10和D14这三个发育阶段中相关组织的轨迹变化规律。

all_papers.title: TargetPrior: A miRNA-Signature Embedded Evolutionary Learning Framework for Prioritizing Drug Targets in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Prioritizing therapeutic targets from high-dimensional transcriptomic profiles is hindered by the underdetermined nature of the p ≫ n setting. While miRNA signatures can inform target prioritization, conventional accuracy-driven methods may yield unstable predictive signatures, reducing downstream network reliability and topology-guided candidate ranking. Results We propose TargetPrior, a stability-aware evolutionary learning framework in which EL-CAML derives reproducible miRNA anchors from relapse-associated transcriptomic variation for candidate target prioritization. In childhood acute myeloid leukemia (CAML), EL-CAML identifies a parsimonious 18-miRNA continuous relapse-risk signature and 10 complementary stability-supported biomarkers, yielding 28 miRNAs for literature-curated miRNA–gene network construction. Benchmarking against an expanded set of clinically and biologically supported AML target references showed stronger early-rank retrieval than network-only and statistical approaches. TargetPrior is presented as a computational proof-of-concept for generating prioritized therapeutic hypotheses, rather than as a universal target-discovery solution. all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：在高维转录组数据中筛选治疗靶点时，由于“p远大于n”这一统计特性导致信息量严重不足，从而阻碍了这一过程的顺利进行。
llm_highlights_zh: 虽然miRNA特征谱有助于确定研究目标的优先级，但传统的基于精确度的分析方法往往会产生不稳定的预测结果，从而降低后续网络分析的可靠性以及基于拓扑结构的候选基因排序的准确性。
结果：我们提出了TargetPrior这一基于稳定性考虑的进化学习框架。在该框架中，EL-CAML算法能够从与疾病复发相关的转录组变异数据中提取出可重复使用的miRNA靶标信息，从而帮助确定优先研究的候选靶标。
在儿童急性髓系白血病中，EL-CAML研究识别出了一个由18种miRNA组成的、能够有效预测疾病复发风险的生物标志物组合，同时还发现了10种与这些miRNA稳定性相关的生物学指标。基于这些数据，研究人员构建了一个包含28种miRNA的基因网络模型。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
在高维转录组数据中筛选治疗靶点时，由于“p ≫ n”的数据特性，目标选择的准确性往往受到限制。虽然miRNA特征谱有助于确定优先靶点，但传统的基于精确度的方法可能产生不稳定的预测结果，从而影响后续的网络分析及候选靶点的排序效率。  

**研究方法**  
我们提出了TargetPrior这一基于进化学习的方法框架。该框架通过EL-CAML算法，从与疾病复发相关的转录组变异中筛选出可靠的miRNA标志物，进而用于优先选择治疗靶点。在儿童急性髓系白血病的数据分析中，EL-CAML识别出了18个与复发风险密切相关的miRNA标志物，以及10个能够进一步验证这些标志物稳定性的生物标志物；最终获得了28个miRNA，用于构建miRNA-基因网络。重复实验结果证实了这些高频表达miRNA的稳定性，而通过对独立的小RNA测序数据集的分析，还发现了不同细胞群体之间的表达差异。  

**实验效果**  
与现有的基于临床和生物学证据的AML靶点识别方法相比，TargetPrior在早期靶点筛选阶段的性能更为优异。该技术更像是一种用于生成优先治疗假设的计算工具，而非通用的靶点发现方案。  

**代码获取**  
相关代码可访问以下链接：https://github.com/NYCU-ICLAB/TargetPrior，并已存档于Zenodo平台。

all_papers.title: AdmixLD: Fast genome-scale inference of ancestry disequilibrium in hybrid zones
all_papers.summary: Abstract Summary Hybrid zones represent powerful natural systems for studying reproductive isolation and speciation. One key genomic signature of genetic incompatibilities and epistatic interactions is linkage disequilibrium (LD) — non-random associations between loci from different lineage backgrounds, generated by selection against maladaptive allele combinations. However, admixture alone induces strong genome-wide LD in hybrid populations, obscuring selection-driven signals. Here, we present AdmixLD, a fast, scalable C ++ tool for genome-wide LD scanning in hybrid zones that estimates LD using partial correlation to control for individual hybrid index. By removing admixture-driven covariance, AdmixLD enhances detection of locus-specific associations and enables genome-scale identification of candidate barrier loci and interacting genomic regions. Availability The software and its code source are available at https://github.com/yzfranci/AdmixLD , and scripts for the data analysis are available at https://github.com/yzfranci/AdmixLDAnalysis

all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 摘要：杂交带是研究生殖隔离与物种形成机制的理想自然模型。
llm_highlights_zh: 遗传不相容性与上位性相互作用的一个重要基因组特征就是连锁不平衡——这种不同谱系背景的基因位点之间的非随机关联，实际上是由于自然选择作用抑制了那些不适应环境的等位基因组合而形成的。
然而，仅混合本身就会在杂交种群中引发强烈的全基因组连锁效应，从而掩盖那些由自然选择所驱动的遗传信号。
在这里，我们介绍了AdmixLD——这是一种快速、可扩展的C++工具，专门用于在杂交区域进行全基因组连锁检测。该工具通过利用偏相关分析来控制个体杂交指数对连锁程度估计结果的影响，从而实现高效、准确的连锁关系分析。

all_papers.title: A multimodal, all-optical platform for linking cell identity to metabolic function in intact tissues
all_papers.summary: REDCAT is a multimodal, all-optical platform that maps metabolic activity alongside cell identity in intact tissues at single-cell and subcellular resolution. By integrating Raman imaging, autofluorescence and high-plex immunofluorescence, REDCAT has resolved metabolic features in normal lymph nodes, uncovered lipid-redox remodeling in lymphoma, and exposed intratumoral heterogeneity, suggesting a use in functional histopathology

all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: REDCAT是一个多模态、全光学的平台，它能够在单细胞及亚细胞水平上，对完整组织中的代谢活动与细胞类型进行同步分析。
llm_highlights_zh: 通过整合拉曼成像、自发荧光检测以及多色免疫荧光技术，REDCAT成功揭示了正常淋巴结的代谢特征，发现了淋巴瘤中脂质氧化还原状态的改变，并暴露出了肿瘤组织内的异质性。这些发现表明，该技术具有在功能病理学研究中的广泛应用前景。
